title: 第26章 买不起
novel_title: 凡人修仙：从废器房杂役开始
content_zh:
功德殿门口的队伍，从台阶一直排到院墙根。

    陈青山到的时候，日头才爬上墙头，队里已经站了百十号人。

    多半是外门弟子和杂役，揣着月俸牌等兑辟谷丹；也有几个练气五六层的内门，腰牌往侧门一亮，就从人堆旁边大摇大摆进去了，不必跟谁挤。

    没人多看陈青山一眼——一个压成练气三层后期的外门弟子，灰扑扑的衣裳，混在这堆人里，跟墙根一块旧砖没两样。

    正合他意。

    他没去排兑丹的长队，绕到殿侧的宝阁。这边清静些，专卖法器符箓，柜台后头立着一块乌木价牌，字是朱砂描的，一行行往下排。

    陈青山抬头看了一遍，心先凉了半截。

    下品储物袋，二百灵石。地火小炉，三百灵石。下品飞剑，八十灵石。灵纹笔，六十灵石。护身符，一张二十五灵石。

    他摸了摸怀里那个小布包，里头是他这阵子东拼西凑攒下的全部家底——拢共二十二块下品灵石，还带着体温。

    二十二块。

    连最便宜的一张护身符都买不利索，买完就得喝西北风。

    宗门真会抢。

    柜台后头的执事是个圆脸中年人，正拿块软布慢条斯理擦一把下品飞剑。见陈青山站着不走，眼皮抬了抬。

    “看哪样？”

    “那灵纹笔，”陈青山指了指价牌，“能不能匀个旧的、便宜些的？”

    执事嗤了一声，把飞剑搁下。“旧的也是五十起。小兄弟，灵纹笔是炼器师吃饭的家伙，描一道纹不带断墨，宝阁里就这一种。你拿六十块买回去，是要炼器，还是要拿它挑灯花？”

    旁边有人笑出了声。

    陈青山没接话，只把价牌从头到尾又看了一遍。他不是来斗嘴的，是来认账的——昨夜他翻来覆去想明白一件事：这条命太薄，想厚一点，就得拿东西往上垫。

    储物袋能藏鼎、藏玄片，省得他天天往砖缝床脚里塞；灵纹笔能练拓纹，省得拿旧笔糟蹋朱砂；小炉能炼器，能闭关。哪一样不是钱。

    可这价牌看下来，他那二十二块，连个零头都凑不齐。

    “不买就别挡道。”执事重新拿起软布，“后头还有人呢。”

    陈青山“嗯”了一声，退开两步。

    穷。

    这个字他认了快二十年，今天又被人当面戳了一回，倒也不算多新鲜。新鲜的是——光认穷没用，得想法子让自己不穷。

    他转身往殿内走。

    功德殿正堂比宝阁热闹得多。一整面墙挂满了任务木牌，红漆写着活计，黑漆写着工钱，弟子们三五成群挤在牌下，伸长脖子挑能干的差事。陈青山在人缝里站定，一块块往下看。
content_en:
The queue at the entrance of Gongde Hall stretches from the steps to the root of the courtyard wall.

    When Chen Qingshan arrived, the sun had just climbed up the wall, and there were already hundreds of people standing in the team.

    Most of them were disciples and servants from the outer sect, carrying monthly salary cards and other materials to redeem Bigu Pills; there were also a few inner sects on the fifth and sixth levels of Qi training. They flashed their waistbands to the side door and walked in from the side of the crowd without having to squeeze in with anyone.

    No one took a second look at Chen Qingshan - an outer disciple who had reached the late third level of Qi training. His dusty clothes were mixed in this crowd, and he was no different from an old brick at the base of the wall.

    Just what he wanted.

    He did not go to the long queue for Dui Dan, but went around to the treasure pavilion on the side of the palace. This place is quieter and specializes in magical instruments and talismans. Behind the counter is an ebony price tag with characters drawn in cinnabar, arranged row by row.

    Chen Qingshan looked up and his heart felt cold.

    Low grade storage bag, two hundred spirit stones. Small earth fire furnace, three hundred spirit stones. Low grade flying sword, eighty spirit stones. Spirit pattern pen, sixty spirit stones. Amulet, a piece of twenty-five spiritual stones.

    He touched the small cloth bag in his arms. Inside was all the money he had scraped together these days - a total of twenty-two low-grade spiritual stones, still with body temperature.

    Twenty-two dollars.

    Even the cheapest amulet is expensive, and you have to drink the northwest wind after buying it.

    The sect really knows how to rob.

    The butler behind the counter was a middle-aged man with a round face. He was slowly wiping a low-grade flying sword with a soft cloth. Seeing Chen Qingshan standing still, he raised his eyelids.

    "What do you think?"

    "Then the spirit pattern pen," Chen Qingshan pointed to the price tag, "can you replace it with an older, cheaper one?"

    The deacon snorted and put down the flying sword. "The old ones are about fifty. Little brother, the spirit pattern pen is what the weapon refiner uses to make a living. It can trace a line without breaking the ink. This is the only one in the treasure pavilion. If you buy it back for sixty yuan, do you want to refine the weapon, or use it to make a fool of yourself?"

    Someone next to him laughed.

    Chen Qingshan didn't answer, he just read the price tag from beginning to end. He didn't come here to quarrel, he came here to settle his score - last night he turned over and over again to figure out one thing: this life is too thin, and if he wants to make it thicker, he has to use something to cushion it.

    The storage bag can hide the cauldron and mysterious tablets, saving him from stuffing them into the brick joints at the foot of the bed every day; the spirit pattern pen can practice rubbing patterns, saving him from using old pens to waste cinnabar; the small furnace can refine weapons and retreat. Nothing is money.

    But looking at the price tag, he couldn't even make up a fraction of the twenty-two yuan.

    "Don't block the way if you don't want to buy it." The deacon picked up the soft cloth again, "There are people behind you."

    Chen Qingshan said "hmm" and took two steps back.

    poverty.

    He has known this word for almost twenty years, and today he was poked in the face again. It's not that new. What’s new is that it’s useless to just admit being poor, you have to find ways to keep yourself from being poor.

    He turned around and walked into the temple.

    The main hall of Gongde Hall is much more lively than Bao Pavilion. An entire wall is covered with wooden task signs, with jobs written in red paint and wages written in black paint. Disciples huddled under the signs in small groups, craning their necks to pick out jobs they could do. Chen Qingshan stood still in the gap between the people, looking down piece by piece.
